newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Crude Outlook - jury out on fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Crude Outlook - jury out on fundamentals.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices moved up strongly Monday as speculative buying on futures markets took the lead, though the fundamental strength of the market remained in question, traders said.
The Brent market appeared to benefit from the expectation of lower June loading programs due to a high level of maintenance scheduled for next month.
Also, much firmer relative prices for crude in Asia in the past two weeks has helped to divert North Sea and African barrels to that region and away from the U.S. market.
The price of near-month West Texas Intermediate/Cushing versus nearby Dubai has sunk from $3.35 a barrel a month ago to $2.00 by last Friday.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James -- the most sensitive sweet marker -- traded Monday morning at a nine cents premium to June WTI/Cushing, after moving at similar numbers most of last week.
Traders said they would be especially focused on the relationship between expected North Sea production cuts this summer and where West African barrels are shipped.
But, Texas cash dealers do not see the trend continuing.
"We can't see the African crudes continue to head east, and when the North Sea barrels start coming up short, then you'll see the Nigerian stuff head over here," said a cash broker in the Gulf.

Some analysts remained skeptical that the rally could be sustained. "If nothing comes out in the next day or two, this thing is setting itself up to get whacked," said Bill O'Grady, an analyst with A.G. Edwards in St. Louis, Missouri.
The Brent system maintenance in June has been known for some time and the main equity holders of Brent blend have covered their shortfall for next month, analysts said.
WEST COAST

Meanwhile on the West Coast, refiners said Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude has become more competitive after the discount fell late Friday to $1.50 below June WTI, continuing a trend since early March when it traded at 80 cents under.
A trader at a refiner in the Pacific Northwest said: "$1.60 is where we want to get something done."

West Coast refiners have bought a steady supply of foreign imports for June, with Tosco Corp dabbling heavily in a variety of LATAM grades including a 360,000-barrel cargo of Cano Limon at $2.97 below WTI.
Arco expects to buy two cargoes of Mesa, a Venezuelan lookalike, though the company declines to give further details.
Imports are expected to hurt spot demand for California light crude from San Joaquin Valley (SJV).

Earlier this month, ARCO officials said they would not limit the volume of crude shippers asked to send along Line 63, which carries heavy and light crude from California's San Joaquin Valley and offshore fields to Los Angeles refiners, reflecing weak demand from refiners.
Spot demand for SJV light, which is blended to make Line 63, have also been weakened by Tosco's foreign purchases, traders said.
Since Tosco has acquired Unocal's Wilmington refinery, the plant's 10,000 to 12,000 barrel-per-day demand for SJV light has been displaced by foreigns, traders said.
--New York Energy Desk (+1 212 859 1620))
